Okay, first an example of the idea to make it clear what I mean. Imagine I think /u/Atko is not a good poster in the announcements sub. I'd like to ban him. I'm free to do so by simply opting into being a mod for announcements. At this point I will never see another post from him and it would be effectively as if he has been banned from my perspective. This will also be true to anybody who 'subscribes' to my moderation for the Announcements subverse.

When somebody subscribes to a sub they will be shown a list of all users who have chosen to moderate the sub and are free to opt in as they wish. The owner of the sub could also select a group of 'recommended' mods that would appear at the top of the list although it would still be up to the user to opt in to them. The list would include things like the moderator's handle, the number of subs they have opted to moderate, their number of 'subscribers', and some indication of activity - perhaps the total number of mod actions they've taken in the past month so you know who's alive and who's not. From this list you would also be able to conveniently click on a mod and see a list of all actions they have taken such as which posts/users they've banned and why. Users would be able to readily access the list at any time for any given sub in order to change which mods they sub to. If you think a particular mod for a sub has gone from doing a good job to not so good job you simply unsubscribe them and they are effectively no longer a mod from your perspective. Disagree? Fine, you can stay subscribed to them.

Users who choose to mod would also have to opt-in to being listed or able to be subscribed to. This is for instance you want to do some small things for your own benefit like banning users, but would rather keep it private. It's basically a sort of peer-to-peer moderation system. Take out the centralized all-or-nothing nature of modding and I think you immediately solve a whole slew of problems.
A simple solution to all modding issues: Decentralize it. Any users can opt into modding a sub, but the effects of such powers are visible only to the user or any who 'subscribe' to them
Much of this could easily be solved simply by having a working "block user" button.

While this would also solve that, that's actually in no way what this is targeting.

This is related to the current moderation issues as mentioned by Atko. The one and only reason moderation issues even exist is because people are forced to 'subscribe' to singular centralized mods. This system, along with allowing users to enhance their own experience more easily, also completely gets rid of moderation related issues.
